title: p256-ecdlp: odd-lift half-table BSGS with byte-radix local pages

claims.statement: On the exact protected NIST P-256 profile, given only Q=[x]P, the deterministic cold odd-lift algorithm in proof.md recovers every canonical scalar x in [0,r), including x=0, with success probability exactly 1. The positive odd baby table stores m=2^127 points [2j+1]P. The giant stream has length h=ceil(r/2^128). The unique odd lift z=x if x is odd and z=x+r if x is even satisfies z=(2i+1)2^128 +/- (2j+1). Full y selects the sign; at most two charged scalar verifications accept the reduced candidate. Baby and giant records are packed 32 to a 16384-byte page and ordered inside that page by a stable 32-pass byte radix through 256 ports of capacity 4, using 16-bit local offsets only. Sorted pages are then merged by a complete 16-ary local-memory tree of height at most 32. There is no flat wide-address array. Jacobian generation keeps the chain projective, so each 1024-point batch exposes every Z before the single inversion. Total scalar AArch64 instruction work T=28068769515497374754164342230842034976561602 satisfies T < 1000*2^(1348/10) and (6/5)T < 1000*2^(1348/10). The submitted score is 1348/10. Preprocessing is the baby side plus setup, 9276403576395011358628708835736690067785068 instructions, below 1000*2^134 target units, and is included in T with no reuse credit. Peak storage is 278759314981632789269196478408104519892992 bytes, below 2^143. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. No random walk, index calculus, occupancy heuristic or uncharged advice is used. This is analytic accounting, not a production run.

experiments.purpose: Exhaustively check the odd-lift decomposition and unique reduction on a small odd additive group, and check that a 256-port capacity-4 byte radix sorts a 32-record page. This does not establish production curve behaviour, memory bounds or instruction costs.
